title: Self-attention computational advantage conditional on sequence length relative to dimension
description: The paper notes that self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers only when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d. For longer sequences where n exceeds d, this computational advantage diminishes, though the authors note this is typically not the case for sentence representations in machine translation.
canonical_description: self-attention computational advantage over recurrence depends on sequence length being smaller than representation dimension

evidence.anchor: when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d
evidence.quote: In terms of computational complexity, self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length $n$ is smaller than the representation dimensionality $d$, which is most often the case with sentence representations used by state-of-the-art models in machine translations, such as word-piece [CITE:wu2016google] and byte-pair [CITE:sennrich2015neural] representations.
